rows.howToFix: Remove the distributor cap and inspect for carbon tracking, burned terminals, moisture, and any oil contamination; if oil is present inside the cap, replace the distributor shaft seal/O-ring at the same time or the new ignition parts will fail again. Replace the cap and rotor with quality OEM or Bosch parts, clean the mating surfaces, inspect the plug wires for corrosion or high resistance, and verify base ignition performance by checking for a smooth idle and no misfire under load after installation. On 1993-1995 models with the distributor driven off the exhaust cam, seal leakage is common and should be addressed during service. Typical parts cost is about $40-$120 for the cap and rotor and $10-$25 for the seal, with total repair cost usually running $150-$350 at an independent shop.
